definition: The MLP inside each transformer block, usually expanding the hidden dimension 3-4x, applying a nonlinearity, and projecting back.
details: The MLP inside each transformer block, usually expanding the hidden dimension 3-4x, applying a nonlinearity, and projecting back. Modern LLMs use gated variants (SwiGLU: SiLU-gated linear units), which improve quality per parameter. Research on interpretability suggests FFNs act as key-value memories storing much of the model's factual knowledge.

explainer.lead: SwiGLU is a gated variant of the MLP inside each transformer block, using SiLU-gated linear units. It matters because modern LLMs use such gated variants to improve quality per parameter.

tiers.eli5: Think of a filter that lets some signals through more strongly than others, helping the model store and recall facts more efficiently.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers replace the standard MLP nonlinearity with SwiGLU to get better quality per parameter in modern LLMs. A pitfall is that the MLP, including gated variants, also acts as a key-value memory storing much of the model's factual knowledge, so changes affect recall.
tiers.paperLevel: The MLP inside each transformer block usually expands the hidden dimension 3-4x, applies a nonlinearity, and projects back; SwiGLU uses SiLU-gated linear units. Interpretability research suggests FFNs act as key-value memories storing much of the model's factual knowledge.

explainer.example: In a transformer block, the MLP expands the hidden dimension by 3-4x, applies a SwiGLU nonlinearity, and projects back—improving quality per parameter compared with a non-gated MLP.
